title: How to Prepare a Mobile App Store Launch
h1: How to prepare a mobile app store launch
description: Prepare an app store launch: developer accounts, listing text, screenshots, policies, testing, review rules, marketing plan and what to ask your developer.
intro: Finishing the code is only part of launching a mobile app. The app stores have their own accounts, rules, listing pages and review steps, and mistakes can delay your launch by days or weeks. A little preparation makes the release smooth. This article explains what to arrange before submitting an app, who should own which accounts and how to plan the first weeks after release.

faq.q: Who should own the developer accounts?
faq.a: You should. Create the store accounts in your own business name and give the developer access, so the app stays yours.

faq.q: How long does store review take?
faq.a: It varies and can change over time. Allow several days, and more for a first release or if changes are requested.

faq.q: What does a store listing need?
faq.a: A name, description, screenshots, an icon, a category, contact details, a privacy policy and answers about what data the app collects.

faq.q: Why might an app be rejected?
faq.a: Common reasons include broken features, missing privacy information, misleading descriptions or not following the platform's design and payment rules.
